newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq warns Turkey over U.S.-led allied force.
newsitem.headline: Iraq warns Turkey over U.S.-led allied force.

text.p: Iraq's government newspaper on Wednesday warned Turkey that bilateral ties would be damaged if Ankara renewed the mandate for a U.S.-led air force patrolling northern Iraq.

"We urge them (the Turks) to stop anything that harms Iraq or encroaches upon its sovereignty and to put an end to the illegal task of the infamous 'Provide Comfort'," al-Thawra newspaper said in a front-page editorial.

Baghdad has long demanded that Ankara revoke permission for the U.S., British and French planes to be based in Turkey. The operation polices a no-fly zone for Iraqi planes in northern Iraq to protect Iraqi Kurds from possible attack.

Iraq was Turkey's third biggest trade partner before economic sanctions were imposed on Baghdad for the invasion of Kuwait in 1990, and Ankara is hoping for a revival of business under the U.N. brokered deal that allows Iraq to sell limited amounts of oil to buy humanitarian goods.

This week Turkey and officials from the countries involved in Operation Provide Comfort were meeting to discuss possible changes to the mandate, in force since 1991 when Iraqi troops crushed a brief Kurdish rebellion after the Gulf War ended Iraq's occupation of Kuwait.
Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan last week predicted an end to the allied air operations in northern Iraq but only minor alterations, such as a name change, are expected.

The operation already lost some effectiveness four months ago when one Kurdish faction received backing from Iraqi troops in Kurdish infighting. The allies had to scrap Provide Comfort's ground operations in the region and evacuated staff but the air patrol operations have continued.
